content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to control an analog motor valve with two setpoints: one for normal temperature at 20°C and another for high temperature at 40°C triggered by a switch. I attempted using two PI blocks, but it seems I can’t connect both to the same analog output. How should I approach this?
Which [product_name] module do you have? If your [product_name] supports it, you can use an analog multiplexer block. I’ve attached an example.

Thanks for the solutions, they work great. I’m planning to buy the [product_name] version without display, add an external display, a 2-channel analog input module for PT sensors, a 2-channel analog output, and an 8 digital output module. I have another question: I need to add an anti-freeze function to the same analog output. The anti-freeze sensor is a digital input, and whenever the input is active, the analog output should be set to maximum, regardless of all other PI or analog functions. This heating setup is for a ventilation system, where the old control unit is failing and spare parts aren’t available, so I want to prepare the program before swapping out hardware.

You can set two setpoints (refer to example 190B: Setpoint switching) using an analog multiplexer and the reference button. If a frost alarm occurs, switch the multiplexer to output a fixed max value, e.g., 1000. Note: [product_name] handles analog signals internally in a 0-1000 range. 0 equals 0V (or 0mA), and 1000 equals 10V (or 20mA) at the analog output. Sending a value of 1000 means you’ll get 10V (or 20mA) on that output.

Thanks for the help. One last thing: In the same setup with two setpoints and anti-freeze, can I add another PT100 sensor inside the supply air channel, so I can control the maximum temperature of the air being blown into the room? The main analog input is a PT100 for measuring room temperature.
If I understand you correctly: You want to know if it's possible to change the control value between room temperature and supply air duct temperature? If so, yes, you can do this.

Not exactly. PT100 sensor 1 is in the room set to 20°C; then I activate setpoint 2 at 40°C, which sets the analog output (motor valve) to max, possibly resulting in a high flow through the heating coil. The fresh air temperature entering the room can exceed 40–50°C. I’d like to add a second PT100 sensor within the ventilation channel to limit the supply air temperature. It may slow the heating process, but it will reduce central heating energy consumption.
Can you share your program file?
The attachment contains an example showing how to delay the setpoint change when switching through an analog ramp.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are aiming to configure a [company_name] control module to operate an analog motor valve with two selectable temperature setpoints, along with an anti-freeze mode that overrides normal operation. There is also interest in integrating two PT100 sensors: one for standard room temperature control and another to limit the supply air temperature, especially useful in a ventilation retrofit. Key challenges include mapping multiple setpoints to one analog output, ensuring a digital override for anti-freeze via a sensor input, and updating logic to support temperature limiting via multiple sensors.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a straightforward configuration solution for managing several temperature setpoints on one analog output, incorporating a digital input for anti-freeze override, and enabling an extra PT100 sensor for supply air temperature limitation—all built into the [product_name] platform.
